title: Spin Polarization Enhanced Photocatalytic N2 Reduction on Chiral Mesostructured Bi2WO6
abstract: Abstract Harnessing the earth-abundant N2 via photocatalysis is a sustainable route to green NH3 synthesis. However, photocatalytic N2 reduction (PNR) remains constrained by the high energy barrier for N2 activation and reduction. In this work, we report that the spin-polarized chiral mesostructured Bi2WO6 (CMB) can facilitate the formation of metastable triplet NOH (3NOH) intermediates, while simultaneously promoting the separation and transport of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby enhancing PNR performance. The CMB was fabricated via a hydrothermal method using tartaric acid as a symmetry-breaking agent. Under sacrificial-agent-free conditions, the NH3 yield of 1325.5 μmol gcat–1 h–1 was achieved, representing a 4.7-fold enhancement over the best values reported for Bi- and W-based catalysts. The pronounced accumulation of the *NOH intermediate, a key precursor to NH3, is speculated to originate from the 3NOH intermediate, driven by the spin polarization of CMB. This work reveals the critical role of spin polarization in regulating triplet reaction intermediates and charge-carrier dynamics during N2 reduction, providing an effective strategy for the design of advanced photocatalysts for sustainable NH3 synthesis.

title: Record‐High Birefringence Achieved by Linearly Extended π‑Conjugated Building Blocks in Metal‐Free Sulfate
abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of birefringent materials is critical for next‐generation integrated photonics, yet conventional systems face intrinsic limitations in birefringence magnitude. Sulfate crystals offer a promising platform but have been hindered by their dependence on specific metal cations and insufficient optical anisotropy. Here, we report a molecular design strategy that overcomes these constraints by employing linearly extended π‐conjugated organic cations as high‐anisotropy building units. Through rational amino‐functionalization of C 12 H 8 N 2 , we engineer the novel cation [H 2 (C 12 H 10 N 4 )] 2 + , which exhibits an exceptional polarizability anisotropy of 156.7 a.u. Using a mild aqueous route, a metal‐free sulfate crystal, [H 2 (C 12 H 10 N 4 )]SO 4 ·3H 2 O was synthesized, which achieves a record birefringence of 0.981 at 550 nm, surpassing all known sulfate birefringent materials and outperforming commercial benchmarks and setting a new performance standard for birefringent sulfates. Structural analysis reveals that the cations align via hydrogen‐bond‐directed assembly with sulfate tetrahedra into a quasi‐two‐dimensional anisotropic structure, thereby maximizing the macroscopic optical response. This study demonstrates that incorporating linearly extended π‐conjugated organic building blocks into sulfate frameworks sever as a robust strategy for discovering highly birefringent crystals.

title: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. Combining X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, we reveal the different templating properties of the mono- and ditopic cations on the long-range structural order and local coordination environment, identifying an unreported phase transition for DABSnI4. The constrained molecular motions in the DJ perovskite provide an increased structural rigidity that also suppresses vibrational modes of the inorganic sublattice. The consequent lower exciton–phonon coupling and exciton binding energy, reduced defectivity, and modulation of the exciton recombination dynamics create favorable conditions to stabilize the population inversion and achieve amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in DABSnI4, in net contrast with BA2SnI4 where ASE could not be obtained. This work highlights that Dion–Jacobson perovskites can create more rigid structural environments with positive feedback on the photophysical properties, providing a simple but effective design strategy for the synthesis of improved materials for optoelectronic applications.

title: An IscS Persulfide Donates the Sulfur for Ribosomal Protein uL16 Thioamidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Posttranslational sulfur incorporation into peptide backbones is increasingly reported. These efforts broaden our understanding of thioamides, which have distinct conformational and hydrogen‐bonding properties compared with amides. YcaO‐catalyzed thioamidation of the ribosomal protein uL16 reportedly occurs across thousands of Pseudomonadota. Here, we identify the cysteine desulfurase IscS, a crucial component of iron–sulfur cluster assembly, as the direct sulfur donor for uL16 thioamidation. Genetic deletion, in vitro reconstitution, kinetic analysis, sulfide scavenging, and mutational studies support this conclusion. Our data support a mechanism in which the IscS persulfide attacks the O ‐phosphorylated uL16 backbone amide to form an IscS–uL16 disulfide intermediate. This labile disulfide is rapidly reduced, and the resulting hemiorthothioamide collapses with phosphate release to give the thioamide. IscS binds uL16 with mid‐nanomolar affinity and can be displaced by other IscS‐dependent sulfur acceptors. IscS promotes formation of the 2:2 YcaO–uL16 complex from the otherwise predominant 1:1 complex. Structural and mutational studies identify uL16 residues important for catalytically competent enzyme–substrate interactions. These findings define the sulfur delivery pathway for uL16 thioamidation and reveal an additional role of the IscS persulfide beyond iron–sulfur cluster assembly, suggesting it serves as another nucleophile for YcaO‐catalyzed backbone modification.

title: Structural Softness–Rigidity Mediation Enables Multicolor Emission and Long‐Lived Phosphorescence in Hf/Zr Halides
abstract: ABSTRACT Multicolor fluorescence, typically favored by soft environments, and phosphorescence, which relies on rigid lattices to stabilize triplet excitons, are fundamentally incompatible and hard to coexist within a single material. Here, we report a crown–ether–directed lattice assembly that integrates [HfCl 6 ] 2‒ /[ZrCl 6 ] 2‒ octahedra and DB18C6@M(K + /Rb + ) supramolecular, yielding four unknown organic–inorganic hybrid Hf/Zr halides. Notably, (DB18C6@K) 2 (CH 3 CN) 2 HfCl 6 achieves an exceptional room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) quantum yield (Φ p ) of 54.43%, a long lifetime of 0.8 s, and a visually discernible afterglow persisting up to 6 s. Moreover, these materials exhibit excitation–dependent multicolor emission, producing green and blue–white outputs under 302 and 365 nm irradiation, respectively. This unique multimodal luminescence originates from the synergistic interplay between the balanced soft‐rigid lattice provided by the crown‐ether framework and heavy – atom Hf/Zr centers, which facilitates intersystem crossing, enabling both efficient RTP and tunable multichannel pathways. It has been confirmed by the high–pressure synchrotron angle–dispersive x–ray diffraction and Raman results. Overall, this work establishes a heavy–atom–based structural mediation which may offer a generalizable route to high‐efficiency, multichannel, and stimuli‐responsive RTP materials.

title: RNA Organelles in DNA‐Based Artificial Cells Provide Spatial Aptamer Functions and Enhanced Signal Processing
abstract: ABSTRACT Naturally occurring biomolecular condensates orchestrate key cellular processes by creating spatially distinct reaction environments, yet engineering synthetic condensates that combine structural programmability with spatioselectively encoded function remains challenging. Here, we report multiphase DNA–RNA artificial cells (ACs) that embed functional RNA condensates as organelle‐like compartments within programmable DNA core–shell ACs. A single thermal assembly protocol yields three‐phase ACs comprising a glassy RNA core organelle embedded in a liquid‐like DNA compartment, surrounded by a crosslinked DNA shell. The RNA organelles contain aptamer function, enabling selective protein recruitment and small‐molecule activation, while the DNA scaffold provides independent addressability, modulates RNA‐condensate size, and enhances resistance to serum‐mediated degradation. We further show that RNA chemistry can be used to adjust environmental responsiveness: unmodified RNA organelles undergo rapid degradation in serum and release captured protein cargo, whereas 2′‐fluoro‐modified RNA organelles remain stable for at least 24 h. Finally, by coupling transcriptional modules localized in the DNA core to cell‐free protein translation in the surrounding medium, we establish sender–receiver communication between AC populations and self‐actuating signal processing within individual DNA–RNA ACs. These results establish hybrid nucleic‐acid ACs as programmable, spatially organized systems that couple compartment architecture, RNA molecular recognition, and biochemical communication.

title: Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for the Capture of Nitrogen Dioxide
abstract: Abstract We report the first adsorption isotherm of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Leveraging the dihedral angle (43.6°) of the biphenyl unit in biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarbaldehyde, upon reaction with p-phenylenediamine, a three-dimensional COF, PKU-800, has been synthesized. Powder X-ray diffraction, hyperpolarised solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and modeling collectively reveal that PKU-800 exhibits a triply interpenetrated qtz-type framework structure, which incorporates missing-aldehyde defects (∼8%) and thus pendant amine termini (∼16%). At 298 K, PKU-800 shows remarkable adsorption of NO2 (4.8 and 18.8 mmol g–1 at 0.01 and 1.0 bar, respectively), representing a new benchmark for NO2 sorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm efficient capture of NO2 (from 2500 to &lt; 0.1 ppm) by PKU-800 under both dry and wet conditions, with dynamic capacities of 4.97 and 5.27 mmol g–1, respectively. In situ spectroscopic and modeling studies reveal that PKU-800 combines a robust three-dimensional topology, fully accessible channels, and strong binding interactions at both the imine and amino sites to synergistically trap NO2, which can be converted readily to nitric acid upon reaction with water in air.

title: Spatially Decoupled Cascade Oxygen Reduction on Bi Single‐Atom and Cluster‐Hybrid Sites for Hydroxyl Radical Generation
abstract: ABSTRACT The two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) for H 2 O 2 production and the subsequent in situ activation to ·OH are constrained by linear scaling relationships, making it difficult for a single active site to simultaneously optimize O 2 activation and H 2 O 2 conversion. This work overcomes the trade‐off by spatially decoupling the cascade reaction onto single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid sites and employing photoelectrocatalysis (PEC). Through a ligand‐exchange and pyrolysis route derived from a metal–organic framework precursor, Bi single atoms and clusters are co‐anchored on B‐doped TiO 2 . The hybrid interface thermodynamically optimizes the intermediate adsorption energies to ensure cascade selectivity, whereas PEC kinetically accelerates the H 2 O 2 ‐to‐·OH conversion by supplying photogenerated electrons. Density functional theory and free‐energy diagrams indicate that H 2 O 2 forms at the single atoms and dissociates into ·OH at the clusters, with the relationship between the p‐band center and ·OH yield following the Sabatier principle. The catalyst delivers a ·OH production rate of 250 µM h −1 at neutral pH and remains active over a broad pH range (3–9). Moreover, it enables broad‐spectrum removal of recalcitrant organic pollutants and retains stable performance over 50 h of operation in a flow‐cell reactor. This work offers guidance for designing cascade catalysts at single‐atom and cluster‐hybrid interfaces.

title: Metal-organic frameworks for separation of organic compounds in liquid phase
abstract: Abstract Liquid-phase separation underpins numerous sectors of modern chemical industry, yet achieving high selectivity for separation of mixtures of organic compounds remains a persistent challenge. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), showing exceptional tunability in composition, topology and pore environment, hold unique promise to address this challenge. This review surveys recent progress in studies of MOFs for the selective extraction and purification of organic substrates in liquid phase, with a focus on elucidating the mechanism of selectivity. Function-directed design principles, encompassing tailored bonding interactions, programmable supramolecular environments and pore-confinement effects, are discussed as enabling precise control over transport processes. These concepts are examined across key application domains, including removal of pollutants in water treatment, the separation of structurally similar hydrocarbons in petrochemical refinery and the selective discrimination of daily pharmaceuticals. Opportunities for the next generation of MOF-based sorbents are outlined, highlighting challenges associated with scalability and long-term operational stability, and the growing roles of artificial intelligence (AI)-guided discovery in developing sustainable separation technologies are further projected.

title: Engineering a multifunctional bioactive coordination polymer nanoplatform for inflammation-responsive bone regeneration
abstract: Inflammatory bone diseases are closely associated with impaired osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and excessive inflammatory signaling. Sinomenine (SIN) exhibits anti-inflammatory activity; however, its therapeutic application is limited by poor bioavailability. In this work, a multifunctional nanoplatform (CS-1@CP1@SIN) was constructed for SIN delivery and electrochemical sensing applications. The nanocomposite exhibited a mesoporous structure, structural stability, and improved electrochemical response characteristics. In a TNF-α-induced inflammatory MSC model, CS-1@CP1@SIN improved cell viability, reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-6), and enhanced the expression of osteogenic markers (Runx2, ALP, and OCN). In addition, the CS-1@CP1@SIN-modified electrode exhibited enhanced electrocatalytic activity toward tert-butylhydroquinone (TBHQ), enabling sensitive and reliable electrochemical detection. These results demonstrate that the proposed nanoplatform integrates anti-inflammatory therapy and electrochemical sensing functions, providing a multifunctional strategy for inflammatory bone disease treatment and food antioxidant monitoring.

title: Cooperative Agostic‐Type C─H···Cu, Quadrupolar Cu···CO 2 , and C─H···O/π Interactions in an Ultra‐Microporous MOF Enable One‐Step Methane Purification From Quaternary C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 /CH 4
abstract: ABSTRACT While agostic‐type C─H···metal σ‐interactions are central to organometallic catalysis, their role in gas separation remains elusive. In this study, a robust phosphine‐functionalized ultra‐microporous Cu(I/II)‐organic framework, LIFM‐XYY‐15, featuring open metal sites (OMSs) and rich aromatic pore walls, is designed to enable one‐step CH 4 purification from a quaternary C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 /CH 4 mixture. Notably, LIFM‐XYY‐15 exhibits much higher C 3 H 8 /C 2 H 6 /CO 2 uptakes than CH 4 , showing C 3 H 8 /CH 4 , C 2 H 6 /CH 4 , and CO 2 /CH 4 uptake ratios of 2.46, 2.30, and 3.92 at 298 K and 1 bar, respectively, which are significantly raised to 12.18, 8.59, and 9.89 at 0.1 bar. The separation potentials (∆ q ) reach 22.12 (C 3 H 8 /CH 4 ), 20.34 (C 2 H 6 /CH 4 ), and 43.69 (CO 2 /CH 4 ) cm 3 cm −3 at 298 K and 1 bar, demonstrating excellent CH 4 purification ability from the quaternary mixture. Breakthrough experiments confirm the delivery of high‐purity CH 4 (≥99.9%) with a productivity of 1.39 mol L −1 with excellent recyclability. The in situ single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD), in situ FT‐IR spectroscopy, and molecular simulations reveal that the exceptional selectivity arises from the synergistic interplay of agostic‐type C─H···Cu, quadrupole‐electrostatic Cu···‐CO 2 , and alkane C─H···O/π interactions, which collectively reinforce the affinity for C 2 –C 3 hydrocarbons and CO 2 while disfavoring CH 4 . This work discloses a crucial role of agostic‐type interactions as a powerful yet underexplored design principle for selective hydrocarbon separations.

title: A Scalable One-Pot Strategy for Porphyrin Metal–Organic Frameworks via In situ Linker Synthesis
abstract: Porphyrin metal–organic frameworks (pMOFs) are highly versatile materials for catalysis, energy, and environmental applications, yet their widespread use is limited by the cost and multistep synthesis of porphyrin linkers. Here, we report a one-pot synthetic strategy that integrates porphyrin formation and MOF crystallization, enabling the direct assembly of zirconium-based pMOFs from simple molecular precursors. This approach eliminates the need for linker isolation and purification, significantly reducing synthetic complexity and resource consumption. The method is demonstrated for the benchmark framework PCN-224 and its zinc metalloporphyrin analogue, yielding crystalline, porous materials at multigram scale. Notably, the resulting materials exhibit enhanced mesoporosity, which improves mass transport and enables superior adsorption of large organic dyes, despite lower BET surface areas compared to conventionally synthesized analogues. Importantly, we further demonstrate the generality of this approach by synthesizing USTC-9(Fe), a framework with distinct metal nodes and porphyrin linker geometry. This work establishes a versatile platform for coupling complex linker synthesis with framework assembly, offering a sustainable and scalable route to functional pMOFs and broadening the scope of in situ linker formation in reticular chemistry.

title: Unlocking the Interfacial Activity of Insoluble Lithium Salts for Stable Lithium Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Employing functional lithium salts in electrolytes is an effective strategy to suppress anode instabilities and sluggish charge‐transfer kinetics in lithium batteries. However, high solubility requirements intrinsically exclude a broad class of promising, high‐lattice‐energy inorganic salts for carbonate electrolytes. Here, we establish an immobilized functional platform (IFP) by deploying insoluble lithium salts with strong Lewis‐acidic Li + sites directly onto an aramid‐scaffolded separator. This design bypasses conventional dissolution–diffusion limitations, yielding a thin, ionically conductive, LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) driven by regulated interfacial Li + solvation and enhanced anion‐derived decomposition. Systematic screening and 6 Li/ 7 Li isotope tracing identify Li 2 SO 4 (LS) as the optimal IFP candidate (IFP‐LS) owing to its moderate Lewis acidity, superior solvent affinity, and industrial viability. Remarkably, LS provides a finite sacrificial lithium contribution during continuous SEI evolution, mitigating irreversible lithium consumption. Consequently, IFP‐LS separators quadruple the lifespan of Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 cells at 0.7 C compared to bare separators, and deliver 88.4% capacity retention over 2400 cycles in Li||LiFePO 4 cells at 5 C. Scalability is further validated through 100 m roll‐to‐roll manufacturing across diverse Ah‐level formats, adding only 0.163 USD m −2 . This work overcomes the lithium salt solubility barrier and unlocks a vast library of potent materials for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries.

title: Synergistic Regulation of High Dielectric Constant and H‐Aggregation for Efficient and Thickness‐Tolerant Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT While the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs) has advanced rapidly, their sensitivity with respect to active layer thickness hinders industrial fabrication. Herein, a novel acceptor BMD‐6F was synthesized via molecular engineering of L8‐BO, which realizes synergistic optimization of dielectric constant (6.20, 1.5 × that of L8‐BO) and H‐aggregation and thus enriches charge transport pathways, facilitates exciton dissociation, and suppresses recombination. As a result, the PM6:L8‐BO:BMD‐6F ternary OSC delivered a champion PCE of 20.34% at 100 nm, and exhibited excellent thickness tolerance with PCEs of 18.23% (300 nm) and 16.18% (500 nm). This work establishes a design principle for high‐efficiency, thickness‐tolerant OSCs, promising industrial applications.

title: Red Light‐Gated Charge Transfer Enables Trace Oxygen Response in Dye‐Sensitized TiO 2 –Carbon Nanotube Hybrids
abstract: ABSTRACT Light offers a powerful means of activating materials with spatial and temporal precision. However, translating excited‐state processes into chemically responsive electronic function in conductive solids remains challenging, particularly under low‐energy red illumination. Herein, we report red light‐gated charge transfer in dye‐sensitized single‐walled carbon nanotube–TiO 2 (SWCNT–TiO 2 ) hybrids that enables trace oxygen detection. Immobilization of red‐absorbing squaraine sensitizers on TiO 2 domains embedded within a conductive SWCNT network reversibly generates a photostationary charge‐transfer state under 628 nm excitation. Despite the low photon energy of red light, the hybrid architecture supports interfacial electron injection into TiO 2 and hole accumulation in the nanotube scaffold, while remaining electronically dormant in the dark. Interception of photogenerated electrons by O 2 perturbs this light‐induced state and converts excited‐state redox chemistry into a chemiresistive signal with ppb‐level sensitivity. This capability enables continuous monitoring of oxygen depletion in a sealed headspace during food spoilage. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, energy‐level alignment analysis, and charge‐carrier inversion experiments show that O 2 triggers light‐activated changes in SWCNT carrier density. These findings demonstrate that low‐energy optical excitation can gate chemical response in dye‐sensitized SWCNT–TiO 2 hybrids, establishing a design strategy for temporally controlled sensing and photoresponsive electronic function.

title: Biomarker and Bioorthogonality Dual‐Locked Chemiluminescent Probes for Cancer Urine Test
abstract: ABSTRACT Bioorthogonality‐activatable optical imaging activates caged or quenched probes via bioorthogonal reactions for disease diagnosis. Although chemiluminescence enables low‐background detection, it has rarely been applied to bioorthogonality‐activatable imaging. Here, we synthesize chemiluminescent tetrazine probes (CLTZs) by coupling a tetrazine acceptor to a phenoxy‐1,2‐dioxetane donor through π‐conjugated vinylene linkers, enabling biomarker and bioorthogonality dual‐locked activation for cancer urine testing. Unlike conventional chemiluminophores, tetrazine in CLTZs mediates an internal‐conversion‐to‐a‐dark‐state quenching mechanism, suppressing chemiluminescence even after phenolate formation. Strong chemiluminescence is restored only when the phenolate form undergoes bioorthogonal reaction with bicyclononyne (BCN), generating pyridazine‐containing donor–π–acceptor chemiluminophores. This unique dark state enables development of an H 2 O 2 and bioorthogonality dual‐locked probe ( H BCP), emitting only when both H 2 O 2 and BCN are present. By engineering BCN into a cancer‐activatable bioorthogonal urinary reporter ( C BUR) that releases renal‐clearable BCN in tumors, a chemiluminescent bioorthogonal pair ( H BCP & C BUR) is created. This pair achieves in vivo tumor imaging with a signal‐to‐background ratio of 438 and detects lung metastasis in early urinary assays with up to 23.9‐fold signal enhancement over healthy mice. This work provides a molecular design for bioorthogonality‐activatable chemiluminescence toward noninvasive, sensitive disease diagnosis.

title: Topological Engineering of NIR‐II Emissive Conjugated Oligomers With Unexpected Excited‐State Manifolds for Efficient Phototheranostics and Cancer Immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Phototheranostic agents operating in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window hold great potential for precision cancer therapy, yet the rational regulation of excited‐state processes to simultaneously optimize fluorescence and phototherapeutic performances remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report a topology‐driven excited‐state engineering strategy for constructing conjugated oligomers with tailored excited‐state manifolds and multi‐channel excitation dynamics. By precisely manipulating molecular topology, conjugated topological oligomers achieve enhanced light‐harvesting capability and optimized exciton utilization, thereby enabling synergistic regulation of excitation dynamics. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, nanoparticles (NPs) derived from TBT‐3 exhibit 2.8‐fold enhanced NIR‐II fluorescence brightness, 2.7‐fold improved photothermal performance, and 7.5‐fold increased total reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation compared with TBT‐1. In vivo studies demonstrate that TBT‐3 NPs enable high‐resolution NIR‐II fluorescence imaging and efficient tumor elimination. Moreover, TBT‐3‐mediated phototherapy induces immunogenic cell death and enhances antitumor immunity, leading to improved therapeutic efficacy when combined with anti‐PD‐1 immune checkpoint blockade. This work provides a molecular topology‐based strategy for manipulating excited‐state landscapes and establishes conjugated oligomers as versatile candidates for NIR‐II phototheranostics and cancer immunotherapy.

title: Bifunctional MXene-Pd multilayer electrodes enabling coupled electrochemical reforming and hydrogen evolution
abstract: Abstract Conventional water splitting requires high overpotentials, whereas electrochemical reforming offers a sustainable route to produce hydrogen while oxidizing alcohols. In this work, we report the rational design of structurally ordered multilayer thin-film electrodes via electrostatic layer-by-layer (LbL) assembly, employing palladium nanoparticles (Pd NPs) as active electrocatalytic sites for both methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), and MXene as a multifunctional conductive support. The sequential assembly of negatively charged MXene nanosheets and positively charged Pd NPs produced well-defined (MXene/Pd) multilayers, which delivered a high MOR current density of 9.38 mA cm − 2 . This performance significantly surpasses that of other Pd-based multilayer electrodes, primarily due to the role of MXene in preventing NPs agglomeration, providing superior electrical conductivity, and, in the case of HER, contributing its own intrinsic hydrogen adsorption-desorption activity, which synergistically enhances the overall catalytic performance together with Pd. Furthermore, in two-electrode full-cell configurations, peak voltages of 0.9 V with a Pt cathode and 0.65 V with a (MXene/Pd) cathode were achieved, both below the theoretical water-splitting voltage of 1.23 V. The cooperative integration of Pd and MXene thus maximizes both methanol oxidation and hydrogen evolution, presenting a viable alternative to Pt-based catalysts. This study highlights the potential of LbL-engineered hybrid electrodes as a scalable and high-performance platform for electrochemical reforming and clean energy applications.

title: Weak Interaction-Driven Self-Assembly of Low-Hygroscopicity Oxidizers for Biocidal Nanoenergetic Materials with Favorable Ignition Performance
abstract: Abstract Iodine pentoxide (I2O5) features a high elemental iodine content, and the composite materials formed with nano-aluminum (n-Al) exhibit both high reactivity and abundant gas generation. However, the n-Al/I2O5 system suffers from a long ignition delay and strong hygroscopicity of I2O5. In this work, a novel iodine-rich energetic oxidizer, [C2H10N2](H2I3O9)2 (EAI-2), was designed and synthesized via weak interaction-driven self-assembly, achieving an ultralow hygroscopicity of ≤0.06% and a high iodine content of 68.26%. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed that the supramolecular architecture was stabilized by cooperative halogen bonds (I···O) and hydrogen bonds (N−H···O). These cooperative interactions effectively shielded the samples from moisture adsorption. Three n-Al/EAI-2 composites were prepared via physical mixing (PM), cooling crystallization (CC), and spray antisolvent (SA) methods. Systematic characterizations demonstrated that the preparation method profoundly affected the crystal morphology, interfacial contact, and mixing uniformity of the composites. SA-n-Al/EAI-2 exhibited the most intimate interfacial contact, attributed to the rapid nucleation and constrained crystal growth during the antisolvent-induced precipitation. Consequently, SA-n-Al/EAI-2 displayed superior sensitivity performances, with an impact sensitivity of &gt;30 J, a friction sensitivity of 108 N, and a flame sensitivity of 7.9 cm, outperforming CC-n-Al/EAI-2. The ignition delay of SA-n-Al/EAI-2 (337.6 ms) was significantly shorter than that of n-Al/I2O5 (1039.6 ms) and PM-n-Al/EAI-2 (946.7 ms), demonstrating the critical role of interfacial engineering in energy release behavior. This study elucidates the relationship between crystallization methodology, supramolecular structure, and energetic performance, providing a crystal-engineering strategy for the design of advanced nano-thermites.

title: Supramolecular Assembly of Photoresponsive Molecular Amphiphile for Functional Soft Matter
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles, obtained by incorporating amphiphilic moieties on a photoresponsive core, effectively bridge synthetic organic molecules with functional photoresponsive soft matters across multiple length‐scales in aqueous media. Well‐established molecular design strategies and principles have been identified for exquisitely designing versatile photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles and systematically programing both structures and functions across multiple length‐scales to obtain mesoscopic and even macroscopic properties. The thrive of photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles drastically expand the potentiality by offering plenty opportunities for their utilization in various fields. Here, we summarize the increasingly enriched applications of photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles according to different aqueous environment (water‐containing interfaces, solution states, and macroscopic soft scaffolds), describing how photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles were designed to fit in varieties of fascinating applications by inducing photoresponsive propensities into complex aqueous media and constructing functionality with versatile photoresponsive moieties.

title: Interfacial Cofactor Recycling Electroenzymatic Platform for Endergonic CO2 Reduction
abstract: Abstract To overcome the thermodynamic barrier of “NADH-dependent CO2 reduction”, we developed a bioelectrosynthesis platform via the co-immobilization of CO2 reductase (CR) and diaphorase (DP) on a graphite electrode. A strategic protein engineering approach, utilizing carbon-specific solid-binding peptides (SBPs), enabled oriented enzyme assembly to facilitate efficient interfacial electron transfer. Among the variants, the dual-functionalized system—comprising C-terminal SBP-fused CR and N-terminal ferredoxin (Fd)/SBP-fused DP3—exhibited superior bioelectrocatalytic synergy, achieving a current density of –193.35 µA cm–2. At –0.5 V (vs Ag/AgCl), this integrated interface effectively drove the endergonic reduction process, maintaining continuous cofactor regeneration with an electron transfer efficiency of 39.2%.

title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
abstract: Abstract Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe 48 Mn 32 Co 10 Cr 10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
abstract: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo12, which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo12-based PE-skin (1) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device (1A) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1-based facial-computer interface (1B) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals and advanced human-computer interaction. Piezoelectric materials enable bioelectronic sensing by converting mechanical stimuli into electrical signals. Xu et al. introduce intrinsically flexible polyoxometalate-based subnanowires and demonstrate their scalable integration into wireless wearable systems for human physiological monitoring.

title: One‐Pot Construction of Amine‐Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks via Photoredox‐Catalyzed Reductive Amination
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic synthesis, as a green and efficient approach to organic synthesis, has been widely adopted in various organic transformations; however, its application in the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains in the early stages of development. Moreover, to date, no photocatalytic approach has been employed for the synthesis of amine‐linked COFs, which feature a higher density of basic sites and demonstrate enhanced stability. Herein, we report a novel one‐pot photoredox‐catalyzed reductive amination strategy for the synthesis of amine‐linked COFs under ambient conditions for the first time. Based on this strategy, a series of amine‐linked COFs were synthesized. Among these materials, DT‐Am‐COF exhibits excellent photocatalytic activity and demonstrates high efficiency as a catalyst for the light‐driven oxidative hydrogenation of arylboronic acids and oxidation of sulfides. This study not only presents an effective method for the synthesis of amine‐linked COFs, but also opens new insights into their preparation.

title: Interfacial Confinement Enables Dual Hosting of Sulfur Mustard and Mustard Sulfoxide in NU-1000
abstract: Abstract Zirconium-based metal–organic frameworks have emerged as promising materials for the capture and detoxification of chemical warfare agents, but the molecular mechanism by which a hierarchical MOF differentiates a hydrophobic reactant from its oxidized product remains incompletely understood. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations, grand-canonical Monte Carlo adsorption calculations, and periodic density functional theory to examine the dual-hosting behavior of NU-1000 toward sulfur mustard (HD) and mustard sulfoxide (HDO). Rather than treating NU-1000 only as an adsorbent or oxidation catalyst, we resolve how its internal micropore, mesopore, and c-pore interfaces impose distinct confinement environments on reactant and product species. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that HD binds most favorably in the c-pore region, with a binding energy of approximately −12.5 kcal/mol, and similarly favorable stabilization in confined micropore environments, whereas substantially weaker binding is observed in the mesopore. Molecular dynamics simulations also reveal sharply different pore residence patterns: HD localizes predominantly in micropores, occupying this region for ∼80% of the trajectory, while HDO samples larger pore environments more broadly, with ∼45% mesopore and ∼34% c-pore occupancy. This pore-selective behavior persists under mixed HD/HDO coadsorption conditions, demonstrating that reactant–product differentiation is intrinsic to the NU-1000 pore network rather than an artifact of isolated single-component simulations. Radial distribution functions further show that HD is stabilized by dispersion-dominated confinement and weak halogen–hydrogen contacts, whereas HDO is governed by more localized, orientation-dependent interactions with hydrated zirconium node sites. These interaction differences produce a pronounced transport asymmetry, with HDO exhibiting a self-diffusion coefficient of 10.6 ± 2.11 × 10–10 m2/s compared with 0.5 ± 0.09 × 10–10 m2/s for HD at comparable loading. The results identify NU-1000 as a dual-function molecular host that couples reactant retention with product mobility, providing an interface-level mechanism relevant to selective CWA detoxification and confined transport in hierarchical porous catalysts.

title: Homochiral Evolution from Self-Assembly of Chiral Block Copolymers
abstract: Abstract A block copolymer containing a chiral block is referred to as a chiral block copolymer, which can form a helical phase (H*) in diblock copolymers and an alternating gyroid phase (GA) in triblock terpolymers with controlled chirality from self-assembly, as evidenced by electron tomography. Polylactide-containing chiral block copolymers can be used as a representative system for the investigation of homochiral evolution from molecular chirality examined by electronic circular dichroism (ECD) to conformational chirality examined by C═O vibrational circular dichroism (VCD), and finally to phase chirality characterized by electron tomography, with C–O–C VCD providing insight into interchain chiral interactions. The intra- and interchain contributions should be evaluated in the context of the specific molecular structure and sample conditions. By taking advantage of noncovalent chirality induction, it is feasible to introduce a chiral bias by associating a chiral dopant with an achiral block, giving H* with controlled chirality from an achiral block copolymer. This Viewpoint highlights the fundamental principles, providing perspectives on the design of chiral soft materials for device applications.

title: Sustainable design of metal-lignin coordination complexes for next-generation energy and environmental applications
abstract: Lignin forms coordination complexes with multivalent metal ions, bridging lignin chemistry with metal nanomaterials for diverse applications. However, developing metal-lignin coordination complexes (MLCC) remains hindered by critical challenges, including structural heterogeneity, uncontrolled aggregation, and the complexity of tailoring coordination microenvironments. This review elucidates the advancements and emerging trends in the synthetic strategies, structural modulation and property regulation of MLCC, with a focus on the interplay between lignin and metal ion coordination. The coordination principles between lignin and metal ions for MLCC preparation via co-precipitation, self-assembly, and templating are initially discussed. Following this, emphasis is placed on the different functionalization regulations that can be conducted by lignin and metal ions in MLCC according to their different types, which mainly include micro/macro morphology regulation, and carbon material preparation. Subsequently, the applications of MLCC in energy conversion and storage, and environmental applications are discussed. Finally, the challenges and future directions of MLCC are envisioned. This review bridges lignin chemistry with metal nanomaterials, providing insights and pathways toward enhancing the performance of existing lignin-based functional materials across diverse applications.

title: Designing an Emulsion-Templated Pentablock Copolymer for Hierarchical Porosity
abstract: Abstract Hierarchically porous polymers integrate macro-, meso-, and micropores to enhance mass transport, diffusion, and specific surface area, making them attractive for applications in filtration, separation, and storage. Here, an innovative pentablock copolymer (PBC), synthesized using sequential atom transfer radical polymerizations (ATRPs), was designed so that each block would contribute a distinct level of porosity to a hierarchically porous monolith. First, a triblock copolymer with hyper-cross-linkable polystyrene (PS) end-blocks was synthesized from a macroinitiator based on a degradable polycaprolactone (PCL) diol. The PBC was then synthesized by adding cross-linkable poly(glycidyl methacrylate) (PGMA) end-blocks to the PS-b-PCL-b-PS. The PBC was used to form the external phase of an oil-in-oil medium internal phase emulsion and then cross-linked via the PGMA’s epoxide groups to generate a macroporous monolith. Selectively etching the sacrificial PCL midblocks in the emulsion-templated monolith generated mesopores. Hyper-cross-linking the PS blocks generated micropores and etched some of the PCL, generating mesopores. This multiblock pore-generation strategy enabled control over the hierarchical nature of the porous structure, providing a rational approach to designing robust, tunable porous monoliths for advanced applications.

title: Mechanism-Guided Triple Defense of Solid Deposition Enabling Durable Electrochemical Cement Clinker Precursor Synthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrifying cement production offers a viable pathway to decarbonize one of the world’s most CO2-intensive industries. Electrochemical synthesis of cement clinker precursors enables low-temperature manufacturing but is constrained by solid deposition, reactor blockage, and voltage instability that limit durability. Here, we identify the dominant deposition-induced degradation pathway in a three-chamber electrochemical reactor and develop mechanism-guided mitigation strategies. The voltage rise is governed by ohmic loss from Ca(OH)2 accumulation in the middle chamber, while coupled experiments and simulations reveal that hydrodynamic heterogeneity creates low-velocity zones that promote particle retention. Guided by these insights, a synergistic triple-defense strategy integrating flow-field redesign, electrolyte regulation, and surface wettability control suppresses deposition at multiple origins. As a consequence, these coordinated interventions extend continuous reactor operation from ∼1 to ∼9 h without sacrificing Faradaic efficiency. Furthermore, the strategy was validated in a scaled-up reactor with an effective electrode area of 100 cm2, achieving stable operation for 100 h at 5 A (50 mA cm–2). This work elucidates deposition-driven degradation mechanisms and establishes general design principles for durable electrochemical reactors for industrial decarbonization.

title: Glycosylated Diarylmethyloxy-Triazines: Facile Synthesis and Aqueous Self-Assembly for Supramolecular Hydrogel Formation
abstract: Abstract Glycosylated self-assembling molecules enable the construction of nanostructures whose surfaces are decorated with saccharides under aqueous conditions, reminiscent of biological systems at both the molecular and cellular levels. Such glyco-nanostructures thus hold great promise as soft materials for biological applications. Herein, we report the facile synthesis of glycosylated diarylmethyloxy-triazines, which serve as new building blocks for fabricating self-assembled nanostructures in aqueous media and forming supramolecular hydrogels. The triazine scaffold enables the protecting-group-free synthesis of glycosylated compounds with reasonable β-anomer selectivity. Notably, both the substituents on the aryl groups attached to the triazine core and the geometry of the glycosidic linkages in the disaccharides strongly influence the hydrogelation behavior.

title: Self-assembly of a giant heterometallic polyoxovanadate with catalytic activity for epoxidation of alkenes
abstract: Abstract The self-assembly of giant polyoxovanadates (POVs) is highly attractive yet extremely challenging, hampered by protonation complexity and structural instability. Here, we obtain the largest POV cluster 1 via self-assembly in aqueous solution, in which tartaric acid serves as a structure-directing agent via synergistic coordination interactions between the metal linkers and the POV motifs. This aesthetically appealing giant compound 1 contains 128 vanadium ions and represents the highest‑nuclear V cluster known in POV chemistry to date. Compound 1 is a tetramer of manganese‐bridged [VV20VIV12(C4H2O6)8(OH)10O66(Cl)]27− units that are unique configurations and potential building blocks. Meanwhile, 1 exhibits excellent catalytic performance in the epoxidation reaction of cyclooctene, achieving 98% conversion and 99% selectivity under oxygen atmosphere. This work not only provides a new topology structure to POM chemistry but also establishes a synthesis strategy for constructing high-nuclear POVs.

title: Alkylene Spacer Engineering for Boosting Circularly Polarized Luminescence in Homopolypeptide Self-Assembly
abstract: Abstract Functional materials with circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) property featuring both high luminescence efficiency and strong chiroptical activity are highly desirable for advanced photonic applications such as three-dimensional displays, optical encryption, asymmetric photochemistry, and biomedical imaging, yet remain challenging to develop. While extensive efforts have focused on engineering chromophore structures and chiral building blocks, the influence of the spacer connecting luminophores and chiral scaffolds on CPL generation remains poorly understood. Herein, we report an alkylene spacer engineering strategy to regulate supramolecular chirality and CPL performance in homopolypeptide-based assemblies. A series of luminescent homopolypeptides were synthesized, bearing an achiral terminal luminophore connected to the backbone through alkylene spacers of varying lengths. By self-assembly, nanotoroid-dispersed aqueous solutions were obtained from these homopolypeptides with photoluminescence quantum yields exceeding 50%. Despite their nearly identical morphologies, the assemblies exhibited markedly different CPL activities. Increasing the spacer length led to continuous enhancement of CPL performance, with the luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) increasing by an order of magnitude from 1.1 × 10–3 to 1.1 × 10–2. Structural characterization and molecular simulations reveal that spacer elongation strengthens the coupling between the terminal luminophore and helical polypeptide scaffold, facilitating more efficient chirality transfer and supramolecular chirality amplification within the toroidal assemblies. Further optimizing the degree of polymerization promotes supramolecular ordering and amplifies CPL activity, yielding an enhanced glum up to 1. 8 × 10–2. This work reveals a previously overlooked role of spacer-mediated chirality communication between the terminal luminophore and helical polypeptide scaffolds and establishes alkylene spacer length as a critical structural parameter for chirality amplification in this supramolecular CPL system, providing new insights into the “molecular structure – supramolecular assembly – chiroptical property” relationship.

title: Supramolecular structuring of nanoparticle ligand shells revealed by liquid-phase AFM
abstract: Abstract Polymer grafts are a ubiquitous component of nanocrystal (NC) ligand shells and impart critical functionalities, including biocompatibility and colloidal stability. Although many techniques have been used for elucidating the supramolecular structure of polymer chains once grafted to the NC surface, few of these are able to provide a complete picture of the ligand shell under experimentally relevant conditions ( e.g ., low polymer densities, various solvent environments). Here, we use high-resolution atomic force microscopy imaging along with coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to directly image polymers grafted onto single Ag NCs in both air and water to better understand the ligand-solvent interactions that dictate ligand shell structuring. For hydrophobic grafts under poor solvent conditions, the grafts self-associate to form a patchy shell, as previously reported. However, for hydrophilic grafts under good solvent conditions, this patchy morphology persists and is observed even for polyethylene glycol-functionalized NCs (i.e. PEGylated) in water. Polymer structuring is also observed amongst assembled NCs, with the formation of polymer bridges forming across patches. These unexpected results suggest that surface patchiness may be more widespread in colloidal NC systems than previously assumed, and this surface heterogeneity could play an important role in governing collective NC phenomena such as self-assembly.

title: Multivalent ubiquitin recognition regulates multiple stages of Tau self-assembly
abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) has emerged as an important intermediate in the pathological self-assembly of Tau, yet the molecular mechanisms that regulate this process remain incompletely understood. Although ubiquitin is a prominent component of pathological inclusions in tauopathies and other neurodegenerative diseases, its presence has largely been linked to targeting aberrant proteins for proteasomal or autophagic clearance. Here, we identify Tau as a ubiquitin-binding protein and demonstrate that multivalent, non-covalent ubiquitin recognition regulates multiple stages of Tau self-assembly. Biochemical, biophysical, structural, and computational analyses identified four ubiquitin-binding elements within the Tau microtubule-binding repeat region that engage the canonical hydrophobic patch of ubiquitin, providing a structural basis for multivalent recognition of mono- and poly-ubiquitin species. Functionally, mono- and poly-ubiquitin suppress Tau condensate formation while enhancing the liquid-like properties of condensates that persist. In contrast, mono-ubiquitin selectively enhances aggregation of the disease-linked Tau-P301L variant under conditions without detectable LLPS, demonstrating that ubiquitin exerts distinct effects depending on the molecular context and stage of Tau self-assembly. Together, these findings establish non-covalent ubiquitin recognition as a previously unrecognized mechanism regulating Tau phase behavior and aggregation. More broadly, they expand the role of ubiquitin beyond protein quality control, with ubiquitin architecture providing an additional layer of regulation over Tau condensate formation, dynamics, maturation, and aggregation.

title: Scrambling-free synthesis of heteroleptic silylium ions by halide abstraction from halosilanes
abstract: Abstract Heteroleptic silylium ions with different substituents at the silicon atom are generally not accessible using established tools for producing such reactive intermediates because substituent exchange reactions occur in acidic media, leading to homoleptic silylium ions with three identical alkyl and aryl substituents, respectively. Here we report a broadly applicable route to heteroleptic silylium ions using halosilanes as silylium ion precursors, which are less prone to that scrambling process. While this deceptively simple method has failed so far owing to the lack of a suitable halide-abstracting agent, superhalophilic halogen-substituted silylium ions enable smooth halide abstraction from a diverse set of halosilanes at ambient temperature without substituent redistribution. Accordingly, this approach provides access to essentially any heteroleptic acyclic as well as cyclic silylium-ion motif from common halosilanes, including trialkyl-, dialkyl(aryl)-, alkyldiaryl- and triaryl-substituted congeners. Computational calculations reveal the mechanism of heteroleptic silylium-ion formation and the origin of the suppressed substituent-scrambling process.

title: Photocatalytic tetrapeptides for enantioselective visible light-induced transformations
abstract: Abstract Research on enantioselective photocatalysis has so far been focused on molecular photocatalysts or large yet easily adaptable photoenzymes. However, both catalysis classes display deficiencies either due to their limited adaptability or their high molecular weight. Here we show that small peptides can bridge the gap between the currently used photocatalysts by combining structural flexibility and low molecular weight. We constructed a small peptide that displays a pyroglutamic acid at its N terminus for substrate recognition. At the C terminus, a thioxanthone-based amino acid was installed to harvest photons and to act catalytically by energy transfer. Two amino acids were sufficient to link the two components, resulting in a photocatalytically active tetrapeptide that was used both for photochemical deracemization and enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition reactions. Our results demonstrate that small peptides with a molecular weight below 750 Da can act as efficient molecular catalysts for enantioselective photochemical transformations.
